<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e01d3473053d2d43f5fca0db98b0409744695a5a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7898a47de302e2d9838b0c4bfdb82ab459739bec`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20413 body and all 8 comments (claims `5867222316`/`5868567572`, reports `5867903998`/`5869246980`, ACCEPTs `5867962277`/`5869268738`, landing note `5868551954`); PR #20434 body, file list and the three-dot diff against `main` (5 files, +153/−42 — identical whether taken at merge-base `24b70859` or against current `origin/main` `e4d3f2ca`); five reads of the check-runs on `7898a47d`. Code read at the head via `git show` only. `audience-posture.ts` and `auth-plugin.ts` are byte-identical between `24b70859` and the head, so the rule the text states was judged against the code that ships with it.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set — nothing moves: right.** The only non-comment source change is the string literal returned by `resolveNoSignInAccountReport` in `boot-sign-in-reachability.ts`. `auth-manager.ts` changes one comment block (the #15587 uniqueness note near line 2295). Exports, the `NO_SIGN_IN_ACCOUNT_AT_BOOT` key, `decideAudienceAdmission`, `resolveEmailVerificationRequirement`, `assertAudienceConfig`, `applyConfigPatch` and the settings binding are untouched. No admission decision, default, or refused value changes.

**Public surface — the shipped boot report, judged clause by clause against the head's code:**

1. "the INVITED login meets the same email-verification rule as any sign-up" — **right.** The `hasPendingInvitation` branch of `decideAudienceAdmission` returns only `{ admit: true, grantPermissionSet: false }` (audience-posture.ts 465–468); nothing in it touches verification. The only rows born `emailVerified: true` are the walled-owner operator stamp (auth-manager.ts 7490–7491, gated by `takeOwnerVerifiedStamp`) and the `NODE_ENV=development` seeded admin (auth-plugin.ts 1972); an invitation-admitted sign-up reaches neither.
2. "Under 'email_domain' verification is always ON" — **right.** `resolveEmailVerificationRequirement` returns `true` for `email_domain` regardless of the declaration (line 198); `assertAudienceConfig` refuses an explicit `false` from any declarant (296–302), so no accepted config can contradict it.
3. "under 'open' it is ON unless the DEPLOYMENT has itself declared it off (emailAndPassword.requireEmailVerification: false, or OS_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false — a false stored only through the settings console is refused there)" — **right.** Resolver: `declared !== false` (199). The constructor asserts with `verificationDeclaredBy: 'deployment'` (auth-manager.ts 1391–1392). `applyConfigPatch` defaults the declarant to `deployment` and keeps the standing opt-out unless a deployment patch re-declares it (4212–4224); the settings binding passes `deployment` only when the settings source for `require_email_verification` is `env`, else `console` (auth-plugin.ts 1706–1707); the env name derives as `OS_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION` with source `env`, locked (settings-service.types.ts 381–382, settings-service.ts 1229/1317). A console `false` with no standing deployment opt-out is refused at audience-posture.ts 304–310 and the prior config keeps ruling; a console `false` beside a deployment opt-out is honoured — so "only" is the correct qualifier, not an over-claim.
4. "under the default 'invite_only' posture it follows that same declaration and is OFF by default" — **right.** Resolver: `declared ?? false`; the verification checks in `assertAudienceConfig` sit inside the `audiencePermitsSelfRegistration` branch, so under `invite_only` any declarant's value applies. The sentence does not say the console can set it there, nor that it cannot; the docs page states it at the same precision ("follows `auth.require_email_verification`"). Not wrong, not harmful.
5. "Wherever it is ON, the invited login is refused EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED at its first sign-in until a mail transport delivers the link" — carried over from the old remedy (b), still pinned by the `#15588/F1` describes (carve-out admits, wiring ON). **Consistent.**
6. Remedy advice: "on a deployment without one, close the posture back to 'invite_only' BEFORE that person registers and leave verification at its default OFF" — **correct and non-harmful.** The carve-out short-circuits before the posture switch, so `invite_only` still admits the invited creation; with nothing declared the resolver wires OFF and the registration yields a session. The added "leave verification at its default OFF" is needed: a declared `true` still applies under `invite_only`. The advice is conditioned on "wherever it is ON", so an `open` deployment that already opted out is not told to close anything. It does not offer the louder alternative (opting out under `open`) — a safe omission, and the boot warning covers that path anyway.
7. Remedy (b) now refers back ("that login meets the same verification rule stated above, so wherever it is ON …"). **The self-contradiction is gone.** Repo-wide grep at the head for the old spellings ("INVITED login too", "every posture other than 'invite_only'", "FORCES email verification ON unless", "third bullet below applies") hits only the new negative pins, the refusal-message regexes in `audience-posture.test.ts`, and one test comment (flagged in ③).
8. The module docblock's invitation bullet restates the same rule and its "second bullet" cross-reference still lands on the hand-written-row bullet (the silencing transition) — **right.** The third bullet, untouched, already carried the `open` exception.
9. `auth-manager.ts` comment (2295–2300) and `signup-existing-address-refusal.test.ts` docblock (30–33): "forces … on by default — always under `email_domain`, and under `open` unless the deployment declared it off" — comments only, **accurate.**

**Pins.** Every positive substring in the flipped `#15588/F1` pin occurs in the head's concatenated literal (checked each, including the split "… and is " + "OFF by default, so no mail transport is needed either"); neither negative regex matches the new text. The new `#20389` describe's four cases each follow from the code read: constructor `open` + `false` honoured (declarant `deployment`); console patch with no standing opt-out refused with the audience-posture.ts:306 message and `getPublicConfig()` still ON (config unchanged after the throw), deployment patch as control; `email_domain` + `false` throws the :298 message at construction; `invite_only` default OFF / declared ON. The helpers it uses (`engineOver`, `wideningAudience`, `invitedSignUp`, `AUDIENCE_POSTURES`, `audiencePermitsSelfRegistration`) exist in the file. The dev's three ablation legs each went red on the scoped test and restored to the HEAD blob — consistent with the pins as read. CI: all six `Test Core` shards concluded `success` on this head.

**Docs alignment.** `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` "Email verification under each posture" (639–660) and `environment-variables.mdx:84` state the identical three-posture rule and the console refusal; the message's long-form pointer still holds. `self-hosting.mdx:580` keeps the "every posture other than `invite_only`" phrasing with the `open` parenthetical — correct, and outside this diff.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/20413-boot-report-verification-text.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `patch` — **right.** The package publishes (`publishConfig.access: public`, no `private`), and the diff changes shipped runtime output (the report string lands in `dist/`), so `skip-changeset` would be wrong. No accept set widens or narrows and no export moves, so the line reading `Clause-②: no` (present at line start in both the changeset body and the PR body, with no arm) is the right declaration and is well-formed; `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The changeset prose restates the same rule and advice as the message — accurate, and it says "Text only: no admission decision, verification default or accepted value changes", which matches ①. This is the only changeset the PR adds; `.changeset/auth-sso-boot-report-gate.md` at the head is already on `origin/main` and is not this PR's. Round 1's `@objectstack/service-settings` patch landed separately in `24b70859`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions: []`** — nothing to answer.
- **Dev deviation (test additions beyond the pin flip; `managerWith` optional argument)** — inside the claimed file; each added pin is a behaviour the code read supports; three retitled tests now say "with nothing declared", which is the true condition. **Right.**
- **Dev deviation (advice qualifiers "on a deployment without one" and "leave verification at its default OFF")** — judged in ① item 6. **Right.**
- **Dev deviation (gate narrowing: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED locally)** — answered by CI on this head: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is hosted by ci.yml `Build Core` (line 2116) — `success`; `check:type-check-debt` by lint.yml `Type Check · debt ledger` (line 6296) — `success`. **Closed.**
- **Dev deviation (AGENTS.md trailer instead of the harness reminder's)** — outside the contract; noted, no action.
- **Dev out-of-scope findings (4 comment-only locations)** — read each at the head. `audience-gate-test-support.ts:17`, `harness.ts:778` and `admin-remove-user-gate-ordering.test.ts:135` explain why fixtures use the invitation lane and are true for the undeclared config they describe; the v18 migration reason text is release history. No operator-facing reach. **Agree with the ACCEPT's acceptance-note disposition (carrier: none).**
- **Reviewer flag, escalated to the seat:** `boot-sign-in-reachability.test.ts:505` (the `#15588/N5` describe comment) still reads "The message's quantifier ("every posture other than 'invite_only'") is pinned elsewhere against the WIRING". That quantifier no longer exists in the message; the dev's stale-phrase count used the longer spelling with the opening parenthesis, so this bare form slipped. Comment only, in a file this PR owns; the N5 assertions themselves still hold (both widening postures and `invite_only` are named in the new text). Not a contract breach and not blocking — a one-line follow-up in the same file, or an acceptance-note entry (carrier: none). The seat decides.
- **Check-runs on `7898a47d` at record time (2026-09-28T11:57:08Z):** 29 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke — path/opt-in skips), 0 failed or cancelled, 2 `in_progress`: `Lint & Repo Gates` and the `Test Core` rollup (all six shards had concluded `success`). Honest reading: no red anywhere, two gates not yet concluded. Readiness waits on those two, as the ACCEPT's own condition already says; this verdict is on the contract, not on their timing.
- **Overlap:** `auth-plugin.ts` untouched, so nothing here meets #20412 / PR #20429; the three-dot diff against current `origin/main` is the same 5 files.
